answer: The fix changed django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py, in `_WKBReader.read()` (the base of `WKBReader`). Before the fix, a `str` WKB (hex) input was passed straight to the ctypes `wkb_reader_read_hex` call, which expects bytes, so it crashed. The fix adds a `str` branch that encodes the string to bytes first and passes the encoded length. I read the current code and did not look up the ticket itself, so this is inferred from that code.

The fix changed django/http/response.py. Before it, pickling an HttpResponse (or a subclass) tried to pickle all of its instance state, including attributes that can't be pickled. These are the `_resource_closers` list, which holds bound methods such as `request.close`, and `_handler_class`, which the handler sets. I worked out the cause from the code and the ticket history, not from the diff, because I couldn't retrieve the commit itself. The change was reverted from Django 4.2.x after ticket #34482, so the corpus code doesn't contain it.

The fix changed django/db/models/functions/datetime.py: Now had no Oracle-specific implementation, so it used CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (a TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE value) that mismatched the DateTimeField's TIMESTAMP type and crashed bulk_create(); Now.as_oracle() now renders LOCALTIMESTAMP instead.

The fix changed django/db/backends/base/schema.py. `_related_non_m2m_objects()` only returned the relations that pointed directly at the altered primary key. With multi-table inheritance, the child's `*_ptr` primary key is also a foreign key that other tables' foreign keys point to. Those second-level columns kept the old type and their constraints weren't dropped and recreated, so the migration crashed. The fix makes the function recurse into the related fields (`yield from _related_non_m2m_objects(old_rel.remote_field, new_rel.remote_field)`), so those columns are updated too. I identified the file and the recursion from the code. I didn't open the ticket or the commit, so I'm recalling that this recursion was the #33462 change.

The fix changed django/contrib/sitemaps/__init__.py (where ping_google() lived; the ping_google management command file was also deleted). What was wrong: Google retired its sitemap "ping" endpoint, so ping_google() and the ping_google command no longer worked and were removed. I couldn't check this against the ticket or commit. The corpus has no ticket text and no trace of ping_google, so this comes from my memory of Django's history plus the fact that the function is absent from this file.

The fix changed django/db/models/constraints.py. What was wrong: BaseConstraint.deconstruct() and the constraint subclasses' __eq__() ignored a custom violation_error_message, so migrations would not serialize it and two constraints that differed only in that message compared as equal. Line 83 is where deconstruct() now emits violation_error_message when it differs from the default. I did not look up the ticket or its fix directly. This answer comes from the ticket title and the current code in constraints.py.

The file is django/core/management/utils.py (find_formatters/run_formatters). The caller django/core/management/templates.py was also touched to use it. What was wrong: startproject/startapp looked up the external "black" executable with shutil.which only after template files had been written, so a file from the template could end up on the search path and be run as "black". The fix resolves the black path once, up front, in find_formatters() and passes it into run_formatters(). I did not have the ticket or the commit, so this is inferred from the current code and its comment at templates.py:113.

The fix is in `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py`. Per the code comment, a sliced union cannot have its parts elided, because when only one part returns a non-empty result, the compiler may be unable to generate valid SQL. I inferred this from the code comment, not from the ticket itself.

The fix changed django/db/backends/base/schema.py (BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.table_sql). ExclusionConstraint.constraint_sql() returns a Statement object rather than a string, so building the CREATE TABLE definition with ", ".join(...) over the raw constraints crashed when adding a model with an ExclusionConstraint. The fix wraps each item in str() before joining. I identified this from the current code, where the str() wrapper is already in place; I did not see the ticket or the original diff.

The fix changed django/db/models/expressions.py. Combined numeric expressions using the MOD (%) operator, e.g. Decimal % Integer, had no entry in the `_connector_combinations` table, so Django couldn't resolve an output_field and raised FieldError for mixed-type operands. The fix added Combinable.MOD to the numeric combinations (same-type, mixed-type and NULL cases), so the result now resolves to e.g. DecimalField. I identified the file from the current source and recalled the ticket and fix from memory; I did not look up the ticket itself.

The fix is in django/core/management/commands/inspectdb.py. I could not verify the ticket or its commit, because the corpus has only the current code and no ticket text or history. The ranked utils.py snippet (run_formatters) is unrelated. This is inferred from the code: inspectdb is where generated models get their related_name. That happens in the used_relations check, where it sets extra_params["related_name"] to "<model>_<att_name>_set". The problem would be that two foreign keys to the same model produced the same default reverse accessor, so the generated models failed Django's reverse-accessor clash check (fields.E304).

The fix changed django/core/handlers/asgi.py (it added get_script_prefix(), which ASGIRequest.__init__ now uses). The bug was that ASGIRequest ignored the FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME setting and took the script prefix only from the ASGI scope's root_path, unlike WSGIRequest, which already honored the setting. I didn't read the ticket text or the commit, so this comes from the code in the repo.

The fix changed django/forms/formsets.py. Before it, the "too many forms" and "too few forms" validation errors in BaseFormSet were hardcoded strings, so users couldn't customize them. The fix added default_error_messages (too_many_forms, too_few_forms) that the formset reads from self.error_messages, so they can be overridden.

The fix changed django/db/backends/base/schema.py. _all_related_fields() returned the reverse related fields from model._meta._get_fields() in a non-deterministic order, so schema alteration code that iterates over them could behave inconsistently. It now wraps the result in sorted(...). I confirmed the current code in the repo, but I did not look up the ticket text or the commit itself.

The fix (ticket #29027) changed django/core/files/move.py (file_move_safe). On SELinux-enabled systems, copystat() raised PermissionError when copying file metadata after moving across filesystems, which crashed the move. The fix catches that PermissionError and falls back to copymode(), ignoring a second PermissionError. I read the current code, which already contains this fix. I did not look up the ticket or the original commit.

The fix changed django/views/debug.py (the ExceptionReporter's get_traceback_frames; the technical_500 templates were also updated to show the new data). Problem: on Python 3.11+, the technical 500 debug page only showed the whole source line for each traceback frame, so it did not point to the exact failing part of the line. It ignored the fine-grained column positions from `co_positions()`. The fix computes start and end columns and adds `^^^^` underline markers (`colno` and `tb_area_colno`).

The fix changed django/db/models/fields/__init__.py, in CharField.__init__. Value._resolve_output_field() returns a CharField() with no max_length for strings. CharField.__init__ used to append MaxLengthValidator(self.max_length) unconditionally, which created a useless MaxLengthValidator(None). It now only does so when max_length is not None. I didn't see the ticket or the fix commit. This comes from the current code, which has that guard, and from my memory of the ticket.

The fix changed django/db/models/expressions.py (ResolvedOuterRef.resolve_expression). Before the fix, a subquery that referenced an outer query's window expression (via OuterRef) was not rejected and failed later or produced invalid SQL; it now raises NotSupportedError ("Referencing outer query window expression is not supported") when the resolved column contains an over clause.

The fix changed django/db/models/expressions.py. Exists() with an empty queryset (one that raises EmptyResultSet while compiling) had no empty-result value of its own, so it fell back to the inherited Subquery behaviour and returned None/NULL instead of False. The fix gave Exists `empty_result_set_value = False`. I didn't have the ticket or commit text, so this comes from reading the current code rather than the diff.

The fix changed django/contrib/gis/forms/widgets.py. What was wrong: BaseGeometryWidget hard-coded map sizes through the map_width/map_height attributes (600x400), so map widgets couldn't be sized with CSS. The fix deprecates those attributes and emits a RemovedInDjango51Warning, advising CSS sizing instead, when they are set or overridden. This is from the code and my recollection of the ticket; I did not retrieve the ticket text itself.

The fix changed django/db/models/sql/compiler.py (SQLInsertCompiler.as_sql). Before the fix, bulk_create() ON CONFLICT SQL was built from the fields' names, not their database columns. Fields with a custom db_column therefore produced SQL that referenced a column that didn't exist, and the query crashed. The compiler now passes `f.column` for both update_fields and unique_fields. I did not look up the ticket or the original commit. I inferred the pre-fix behaviour from the 4.1.4 release note and from the current code, which passes `f.column`.

The fix changed django/contrib/auth/forms.py. What was wrong: UserCreationForm.clean_username() checked for case-insensitive duplicates against the hard-coded default User model instead of the form's own model (self._meta.model). Subclasses with a custom user model crashed because of that.

The fix changed django/db/backends/postgresql/schema.py. When the schema editor ran its "UPDATE ... SET column = default WHERE column IS NULL" step, PostgreSQL deferred constraints were still pending. A later ALTER TABLE in the same transaction then failed with "pending trigger events". The fix appends "SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE" to the update statement (sql_update_with_default) so deferred constraints are checked right after the rows are updated. I did not read the ticket or the commit. I inferred this from the code in that file, so treat the ticket link as unverified.

The fix changed django/db/models/lookups.py, in Lookup.get_prep_lookup(). Before the fix, a lookup that sets prepare_rhs = False, such as IsNull, still had its direct rhs wrapped in Value() when the lhs was an expression like F('pk'). IsNull.as_sql then rejected the wrapped value because it was no longer a bool, so IsNull(F('pk'), True) crashed in filter(). The guard `if not self.prepare_rhs or hasattr(self.rhs, "resolve_expression"): return self.rhs` now returns the rhs untouched. I confirmed that guard in the current code but didn't find the commit diff, so the before/after reasoning is inferred.

The fix (PR 16076) changed django/db/models/fields/related_lookups.py. RelatedLookupMixin.get_prep_lookup() assumed that the lhs output_field of a related lookup was always a relation field with `path_infos`. When you filtered on a transform of a relation field, whose output_field could be a non-relation type, the lookup broke. The fix guards that access with `hasattr(self.lhs.output_field, "path_infos")`. I inferred the exact change from the current code and the PR title. I did not see the diff.

The fix changed django/db/models/base.py, in Model._get_field_value_map(). Before the fix, that method wrapped each instance value in a bare Value() with no output_field. During CheckConstraint validation, a range field's value (e.g. a NumericRange) had no known field type, so it was not converted properly and the check failed. The fix passes the model field to Value as its output_field. I did not see the original diff in the corpus. The "before" state is inferred from the current code.

The fix changed django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py (_filter_prefetch_queryset). Before, prefetching a sliced queryset couldn't be filtered with the `__in` predicate (the slice was applied globally or errored instead of per parent object); it now clears the limits and filters on a RowNumber() window partitioned by the relation field so each parent gets its own slice.

The fix changed django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py (ContentTypeManager.get_for_models()). What was wrong: get_for_models() filtered content types with separate app_label__in and model__in conditions. That matched stale content types from the cross product of app labels and model names, for example app A's model name paired with app B's label. It then called apps.get_model() on those stale rows and crashed with a LookupError. The fix builds one Q(app_label=..., model__in=...) condition per app and ORs them together. I read the resulting code at lines 83-89, but I didn't see the original code or the ticket text, so the description of the old filter is from my memory of the ticket.

The fix changed django/contrib/admin/options.py (BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_foreignkey). Before the fix, the radio_fields branch always set kwargs["empty_label"] to _("None") (or None if the field wasn't blank), so a custom empty_label passed in by an override was ignored. It now uses kwargs.get("empty_label", _("None")).

The fix changed django/db/models/sql/query.py (Query.get_aggregation). QuerySet.aggregate() crashed when an aggregate referenced an annotation that was a subquery, because get_aggregation() didn't wrap the query in an inner subquery in that case. It now tracks `refs_subquery`, set when an aggregate references a subquery annotation, and forces the subquery wrapping.
